phrase.text: An identifier is the name you choose for a variable, a subroutine or a type: it starts with a letter or an underscore and distinguishes upper case, lower case and accents.

runs.text: An identifier is the name you choose for a variable, a subroutine or a type: it starts with a letter or an underscore and distinguishes upper case, lower case and accents.
starts with a letter (including ñ, accented vowels and ü) or an underscore. After that it may continue with letters, digits or underscores. A single-letter name is valid.

blocks.description: Two boxes joined by an arrow: the first character, which may be a letter, ñ, an accented vowel or an underscore, and the following ones, which also accept digits and may repeat. Below, four valid names in green and three invalid ones in red.

caption.text: What may go at the start of a name and what may follow. Digits may follow, never start.

runs.text: Initial alphabet: ASCII letters, ñ, Ñ, accented vowels, ü, Ü and underscore. Following alphabet: the initial one plus the digits 0 to 9. There is no maximum length. A name may not match a reserved word of the profile.

points.text: Starts with a letter or underscore; continues with letters, digits or underscores.
ñ, accents and ü are allowed.
Names distinguish case and accents; reserved words ignore case.
